       { local @a[0..1] = (1,2) if f(); print "n=$n a=@a\n"; }  print "a=@a\n";
       perl: n=1 a=1 2 0 / a=0 0 0      base: n=1 a=2 0 0 (ONE evaluation, WRONG elements)      MAIN: n=3 a=1 2 0 (right elements, THREE evaluations)
  FIX: bind the temporary whenever the let/init path is taken (`@key_cls > 1 || $ld_slice`).

R5 -- Pl/Parser.pm ~4840-4845: `$ld_cl_var` is the flattened TEXT of `(p-cast-% EXPR)`, spliced into every per-group open and into the `(p-setf (p-hslice ...))` assign; no temporary (the Parser2 hoist binds an expression base once to `$__pcl_lbase_N`; this branch does not).
  f5:  our %h = (a=>1, b=>2); my $n = 0; sub f { $n++; \%h }
       { local @{ f() }{qw(a b)} = (10, 20); print "in n=$n a=$h{a} b=$h{b}\n"; }  print "out n=$n a=$h{a} b=$h{b}\n";
       perl: in n=1 a=10 b=20 / out n=1 a=1 b=2      base: dies "Can't localize through a reference"      MAIN: in n=3 (values right)
  FIX: evaluate a non-Symbol base ONCE into a let-bound temporary before the opens and use that name in every macro and in the assignment (the same shape the Parser2 hoist already uses -- rule 11: ONE way to bind a base once).

BAR: f2 + f5 = perl (a side-effecting condition / base runs ONCE); guard rows in local-term-01.t with a COUNTER in the condition / base (the discriminating measurement), inverse-verified; corpus-diff; the sweep (perl-tests/local.t).
